statement: For a positive integer $N$, let $c_1 < c_2 < \cdots < c_m$ be all positive integers smaller than $N$ that are coprime to $N$. Find all $N \geq 3$ such that $\gcd(N,\, c_i + c_{i+1}) \neq 1$ for all $1 \leq i \leq m-1$.

An infinite increasing sequence $a_1 < a_2 < a_3 < \cdots$ of positive integers is called \textit{central} if for every positive integer $n$, the arithmetic mean of the first $a_n$ terms equals $a_n$. Show that there exists an infinite sequence $b_1, b_2, b_3, \ldots$ of positive integers such that for every central sequence $a_1, a_2, a_3, \ldots$, there are infinitely many positive integers $n$ with $a_n = b_n$.

Let $ABC$ be an acute triangle. Points $B$, $D$, $E$, $C$ lie on a line in this order with $BD = DE = EC$. Let $M$ and $N$ be the midpoints of $AD$ and $AE$. Suppose triangle $ADE$ is acute with orthocenter $H$. Points $P$ and $Q$ lie on lines $BM$ and $CN$ respectively such that $D$, $H$, $M$, $P$ are concyclic and pairwise different, and $E$, $H$, $N$, $Q$ are concyclic and pairwise different. Prove that $P$, $Q$, $N$, $M$ are concyclic.

Let $ABC$ be an acute triangle with incenter $I$ and $AB 
eq AC$. Lines $BI$ and $CI$ intersect the circumcircle of $ABC$ at $P 
eq B$ and $Q 
eq C$ respectively. Consider points $R$ and $S$ such that $AQRB$ and $ACSP$ are parallelograms (with $AQ \parallel RB$, $AB \parallel QR$, $AC \parallel SP$, $AP \parallel CS$). Let $T$ be the intersection of lines $RB$ and $SC$. Prove that $R$, $S$, $T$, $I$ are concyclic.

Let $n > 1$ be an integer. In a \textit{configuration} of an $n \times n$ board, each of the $n^2$ cells contains an arrow pointing up, down, left, or right. Given a starting configuration, Turbo the snail starts in one cell and moves in the direction of the arrow, rotating all arrows $90^\circ$ counterclockwise after each move. A cell is \textit{good} if starting from it, Turbo visits each cell exactly once and returns to the start. Determine, in terms of $n$, the maximum number of good cells over all configurations.

In each cell of a $2025 \times 2025$ board, a nonneg­ative real number is written so that each row sums to 1 and each column sums to 1. Let $r_i$ be the largest value in row $i$ and $R = r_1 + r_2 + \cdots + r_{2025}$. Let $c_i$ be the largest value in column $i$ and $C = c_1 + c_2 + \cdots + c_{2025}$. What is the largest possible value of $\dfrac{R}{C}$?
